title: Experiment orchestration: templates and safe exposure for model-version A/B experiments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end A/B experiment orchestration layer for model-version comparisons that teams can launch from the Console or the API. Focus areas: (1) experiment templates for common patterns (canary ramp, steady-state A/B, shadow-only validation), (2) strict exposure controls with per-customer and global caps, (3) sequential statistical checks with automatic gating and rollback, and (4) clear telemetry and CI hooks for model quality regression detection. The feature should enable PMs/ML engineers to configure experiments with a template, choose metrics and hypothesis, set safety triggers, and launch without additional infra changes. It must integrate with existing rollout primitives (traffic routing, model variants, fallback policies) and with Optimize's registry of prompts/evals for deterministic checks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console: new 'Experiment' flow that exposes templates (Canary Ramp, Split A/B, Shadow). 2) API: experiments can be created/updated/deleted via REST with the same options. 3) Exposure controls: default global cap = 5% for first 24h, per-customer cap adjustable, and emergency kill switch. 4) Statistical engine: runs automated sequential checks (latency and safety event rates) with configurable alpha spending; triggers auto-rollback if thresholds exceeded. 5) Shadow traffic: 100% shadow mode that records outputs and latency without serving responses; diff metrics available in dashboard. 6) Telemetry: experiment dashboard with per-metric lift, CIs, sample sizes, time-to-significance estimate. 7) End-to-end tests and at least one production pilot with internal Redwood app.
tasks: PM: finalize template catalog and default parameter values
ENG: implement experiment API and persistent config storage (feature flags + routing integration)
ENG: integrate sequential stats library (alpha spending, Bayesian online) and expose decisions to orchestration layer
ENG: implement shadow traffic pipeline that hashes requests to model-versions and stores outputs in object store
ENG: wire up auto-rollback hooks to routing/fallback policies
DES: UI flows for experiment creation, metric selection, and safety triggers
SRE: alerting and runbook for experiment-induced instability
QA: E2E tests including simulated adverse-variance and rollback scenarios
PM: pilot run with internal search-relevance team and collect feedback
comments: 2026-03-05 - Asha Patel: Ticket created after kickoff with Search team. Initial ask: make it safe for customer traffic and reduce time-to-run controlled model experiments.
2026-03-06 - Marco Hernandez: Proposed default canary ramp: 1% for 2h -> 5% for 24h -> 20% steady. Holding pattern: use 5% global cap until pilot completes.

2026-03-07 - Eng lead (Liya Chen): We prefer a combined approach: Bayesian sequential posterior checks for safety events (sparse counts) and alpha-spending frequentist tests for latency and deterministic metrics. Will evaluate lib candidates (river, pymc, sequential/triage).

2026-03-08 - Design review (Rohit Kapoor): UI mockups uploaded. Must show 'reason for rollback' and a one-click emergency kill on the experiment header. Also a preview of the population allocation curve for ramp schedules.
2026-03-09 - Security (Maya Singh): Reviewed data flow. Shadow outputs retained for 30 days by default and masked in UI. KMS keys required for exported experiment snapshots.

2026-03-10 - Marco Hernandez: Decision log - use Bayesian online estimation for safety event rate (Beta-Binomial posterior) with ROPE-based decision rules and implement Pocock-style alpha spending for latency checks to avoid inflation from peeking. Auto-rollback when posterior probability that variant is worse by >=5% exceeds 0.975 OR frequentist p-value < 0.001 for latency regressions.
